steps.message:
Using hyperpowers:using-hyperpowers — this lands on rung 1 of the ladder (a field name in a response is an interface others call), so I'm flagging the consequence before editing.

The change itself is one line, `routes/users.js:6`:

```js
users.map((u) => ({ userId: u.id, name: u.name, email: u.email }))
```

The consequence: renaming `userId` → `user_id` is a breaking change for every current `GET /users` consumer. `README.md` names three — the web app, the iOS app 3.2+, and the nightly partner export — and states that field names are part of the contract and that changes go through a versioned endpoint. The iOS and partner-export consumers in particular can't be redeployed in lockstep with the API. Nothing in this repo reads the field, so the repo won't tell you it broke; the clients will.

How do you want to proceed?

options.label: Emit both fields
options.description: Return user_id alongside userId in the existing response. Non-breaking, gives consumers a migration window, and userId can be dropped once all three have moved. Slightly larger payload in the meantime.

options.label: Versioned endpoint
options.description: Follow the README's stated policy: leave GET /users as-is and add a versioned variant (e.g. /v2/users) that uses user_id. Largest change of the three; touches routing, not just this handler.

options.label: Rename it outright
options.description: Do exactly what you asked: change userId to user_id in place. Breaks the web app, iOS 3.2+, and the nightly partner export until each is updated. Choose this if those consumers are already being updated in step.
